analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and source, including the surrounding build documentation. The new .github/workflows/ci-dev-hourly.yml grants only its GitHub-hosted dispatch job actions:write and contents:read (head 19–23). It performs no checkout or execution of dev source, uses repository/token values through quoted environment variables, and dispatches a fixed workflow and branch (head 26–37). API errors stop dispatch under set -euo pipefail. No supported token disclosure, source-injection or provider runtime regression was identified. The changelog and docs/developer/build.md additions describe this automation; unchanged release qualification, cache isolation and authorization guidance are not modified controls. No changes directly affect A-001/A-003, T-008, T-041 or T-052–T-058.
The unfinished-run query (head 31–37) is a bounded, non-atomic check, not a strict concurrency guarantee; simultaneous manual invocations can race. Without evidence of an adversarial trigger or security-sensitive overlapping jobs, this is not a security finding.
Integration must inspect dev's .github/workflows/ci-dev.yml and its called plan/test workflows: they are not supplied here. Verify workflow_dispatch selects the intended full suite, preserves runner admission and cache-write restrictions, and does not expose signing/publication credentials or grant release authority merely because a default-branch scheduler initiated it (A-005, A-011, A-017, T-054). Docs additions explicitly depend on that external branch contract. Automatic execution of that target is the material remaining uncertainty, not evidence of a regression.
